correctness.rationale: Starting with the conditional two-state Kolmogorov equations for the phase functional C(t), verified C''+q C'+a²C=0 with initial (1,0) and F=(g+q−iω)/((g−iω)(g+q−iω)+a²). With z=ω², denominator D=z²+[(2g+q)²−2(gh+a²)]z+(gh+a²)² is strictly positive for z≥0; M²=(h²+z)/D and I=(h(gh+a²)+gz)/D. Differentiation yields decreasing quadratic derivative numerators, so an off-center doublet occurs precisely when the central derivative is positive, with the quartically flat zero-frequency merger at equality. Algebra gives threshold A_g(q)=(g+q)^3/(2g+q+sqrt((g+q)^2+(2g+q)^2)) and B_g(q)=(g+q)^3/(3g+2q), and A<B. Both increase strictly in q. For fixed P<Q, H(g)=A_g(Q)/B_g(P) has strictly negative logarithmic derivative: ∂_g log A decreases as its q increases and is smaller than ∂_g log B at equal q. Its endpoint values are 2(sqrt2−1)(Q/P)² and 3(sqrt5−2)<1, so unique positive g exists exactly above stated ratio; a=sqrt(B_g(P)) follows. Independent symbolic derivative/threshold and numerical H monotonic checks corroborate general analytic proof; q is total correlation decay not individual switching rate.
